answer: A positive change I genuinely want to make is to spend less time on my phone and social media. I have noticed that I waste far too many hours [[scrolling]] mindlessly, which leaves me feeling drained rather than refreshed. It usually starts innocently, checking one message, and suddenly forty minutes have disappeared. I want to make this change because I believe that time could be far better spent on hobbies, exercise or real relationships. Even at the dinner table, which is a special time in my family, I sometimes catch myself glancing at the screen, and I don't like that about myself. To do it, I plan to set strict limits on certain apps and keep my phone out of reach during meals and before bed. I also want to replace the habit with something better, such as reading a few pages instead of reaching for my phone. I know breaking such an [[ingrained]] habit will require real [[discipline]]. Honestly, I think reducing screen time would have a hugely [[beneficial]] effect on my focus and mental wellbeing. It would allow me to be more [[fully present]] instead of constantly distracted. I have already started making small changes, such as turning off notifications for most apps, and I have noticed a difference. I seem to get through my work faster, and I actually finish the books I start. I think in our hyper-connected world, consciously stepping back from technology is one of the healthiest changes a person can make.

followUps.q: Has anyone in your family commented on your phone use?
followUps.answer: Yes, my mother, many times! She jokes that the phone is my second sister. She means it kindly, but it did make me realise how much of our time together I was wasting.

followUps.q: Do you think you will succeed in making this change?
followUps.answer: I think so, as long as I am realistic. I don't plan to give up my phone completely, since I need it for work, but cutting down gradually feels [[achievable]].

note: Added how the habit creeps in, family dinner detail and a replacement habit; marked [[ingrained]]; 'present' became [[fully present]].
